revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Patio Pavers
revealWordProblem.text: Claire's architecture firm is laying pavers on a parallelogram-shaped patio for a client. The patio has a base of 16 feet and a perpendicular height of 9 feet. The slanted side of the patio measures 11 feet. Each box of pavers covers 12 square feet. How many full boxes of pavers should Claire order to cover the entire patio?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: First find the area: A = base × height = 16 × 9 = 144 square feet (the 11 ft slanted side is not used). Then divide by the box coverage: 144 ÷ 12 = 12 boxes. Claire should order 12 boxes of pavers.

vocabulary.definition: The space inside a parallelogram. Formula: A = b × h, using the perpendicular height.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El espacio dentro de un paralelogramo. Fórmula: A = b × h, usando la altura perpendicular.
vocabulary.visual: A = b × h; if b = 10 cm and h = 6 cm, A = 60 cm².
vocabulary.cloze: The space inside a parallelogram, found with A = b × h, is the ___.

examples.text: A = 9 × 6 using the perpendicular height
examples.why: Base times the height that meets it at a right angle.

examples.text: A = 9 × 10 using the slanted side
examples.why: The slant is longer than the true height.

vocabulary.definition: A side that leans instead of going straight up and down. It is not the perpendicular height.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un lado que está inclinado en vez de subir y bajar verticalmente. No es la altura perpendicular.
vocabulary.visual: In a leaning parallelogram, use the dashed 90° height—not the slanted side—in A = b × h.
vocabulary.cloze: The leaning side of a parallelogram, which is NOT the height, is the ___.

examples.text: The 10 cm edge leaning across a parallelogram
examples.why: It leans, so it is not the height.

examples.text: The 6 cm straight-up distance
examples.why: That IS the height.

vocabulary.definition: A four-sided shape with two pairs of parallel sides.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura de cuatro lados con dos pares de lados paralelos.
vocabulary.visual: Think of a leaning door — the top and bottom are parallel, and the two sides are parallel, like a slanted rectangle
vocabulary.cloze: A quadrilateral with two pairs of parallel sides is a ___.

examples.text: A slanted four-sided shape with both pairs of sides parallel
examples.why: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.

examples.text: A triangle
examples.why: A triangle has three sides, not two pairs of parallel sides.

vocabulary.definition: Two lines or sides that stay the same distance apart and never meet.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos líneas o lados que se mantienen a la misma distancia y nunca se cruzan.
vocabulary.visual: The top and bottom of a parallelogram never get closer together — matching arrowheads (›) mark one parallel pair, double arrowheads (››) mark the other.
vocabulary.cloze: Two sides that stay the same distance apart and never meet are ___.

examples.text: The two bases of a trapezoid
examples.why: They stay the same distance apart.

examples.text: Two sides that meet at a corner
examples.why: Lines that meet are not parallel.

vocabulary.definition: Any side of a parallelogram can be the base. Once you pick a base, the height must be measured perpendicular (at a 90° angle) to it.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cualquier lado de un paralelogramo puede ser la base. Una vez que eliges la base, la altura debe medirse perpendicular (en un ángulo de 90°) a ella.
vocabulary.visual: Any side can be the base: choose the 10 cm side and b = 10 cm, then draw the height at 90° to that side in A = b × h
vocabulary.cloze: The side of a parallelogram you measure the height from at a 90° angle is the ___.

examples.text: The 12 in side you measured the height from
examples.why: Once chosen, the height is measured to it.

examples.text: Any side, with a height measured to a different one
examples.why: Base and height must be a matched pair.

vocabulary.definition: The straight-up distance from the base to the top.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia recta hacia arriba desde la base hasta la parte de arriba.
vocabulary.visual: A dashed vertical line from the top side straight down to the base, forming a 90° angle — NOT the slanted side
vocabulary.cloze: The perpendicular distance between the base and the opposite side is the ___.

examples.text: The 7 ft perpendicular distance to the base
examples.why: It meets the base at a square corner.

examples.text: The 10 ft slanted edge
examples.why: That is longer than the straight-up distance.

vocabulary.definition: Two lines that meet to make a square corner (90 degrees).
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos líneas que se cruzan formando una esquina cuadrada (90 grados).
vocabulary.visual: The dashed height meets the base at a square corner — the small 90° box is what makes it perpendicular, not slanted.
vocabulary.cloze: Two lines that meet at a 90° square corner are ___.

examples.text: A height meeting its base at 90°
examples.why: They form a square corner.

examples.text: A height drawn at a slant
examples.why: No right angle, so it is not the height.

vocabulary.definition: How much space is inside a flat shape.

examples.text: A rectangle with a triangle on top
examples.why: Two simple shapes joined.

vocabulary.definition: A math rule written with symbols.

conceptIntro.heading: Push further — How do we find the area of a parallelogram?
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. So we go up a level, not up a number: find what is always true, show it a second way, and be ready to defend it with a reason instead of an answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Area of a parallelogram = base × height, where the height is the straight-up (perpendicular) distance, NOT the slanted side — and you can say why it is true, and where it would stop being true.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the parallelogram
workedExample.work: base = 9 cm, slanted side = 10 cm, height = 6 cm
workedExample.workEs: base = 9 cm, lado inclinado = 10 cm, altura = 6 cm

onLevel.correctWork: The height is 6 cm, not the slanted side of 10 cm. Substitute the perpendicular height: A = 9 × 6 = 54 sq cm. Only the straight-up height belongs in A = base × height.
hints: Look at the substitution step. Which number was used for the height — the slanted side or the real height?
The height must be perpendicular (a 90° angle) to the base. The 10 cm slanted side is not the height, so use 6 cm: A = 9 × 6 = 54 sq cm.
onLevel.explanation: The substitution step uses 10 cm, which is the slanted side, instead of the 6 cm height listed in the first step. Only the perpendicular height belongs in A = base × height, so A = 9 × 6 = 54 sq cm.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso de sustitución usa 10 cm, que es el lado inclinado, en lugar de la altura de 6 cm que aparece en el primer paso. En A = base × altura solo entra la altura perpendicular, así que A = 9 × 6 = 54 sq cm.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: La altura es 6 cm, no el lado inclinado de 10 cm. Sustituye la altura perpendicular: A = 9 × 6 = 54 cm cuadrados. Solo la altura recta va en A = base × altura.
hintsEs: Mira el paso de sustitución. ¿Qué número se usó para la altura — el lado inclinado o la altura real?
La altura debe ser perpendicular (un ángulo de 90°) a la base. El lado inclinado de 10 cm no es la altura, así que usa 6 cm: A = 9 × 6 = 54 cm cuadrados.

onLevel.title: Find the Area Error

workedExample.label: Identify base and height
workedExample.work: b = 11 m, slant side = 8 m, h = 6 m
workedExample.labelEs: Identifica la base y la altura
workedExample.workEs: b = 11 m, lado inclinado = 8 m, h = 6 m

onLevel.correctWork: The height is 6 m, not the slant side of 8 m. A = 11 × 6 = 66 sq m. Always use the perpendicular height, not the slanted side.
hints: Look at Step 3. Which value should be used for h — the slant side or the height?
The height must be perpendicular to the base. The slant side is not the height.
onLevel.explanation: The Substitute step plugs in the 8 m slant side for h, but the first step already labeled the height as 6 m. The slant side is longer than the true straight-up distance, so the correct area is A = 11 × 6 = 66 sq m.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso Sustituir mete el lado inclinado de 8 m como h, pero el primer paso ya había marcado la altura como 6 m. El lado inclinado es más largo que la distancia vertical real, así que el área correcta es A = 11 × 6 = 66 sq m.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: La altura es 6 m, no el lado inclinado de 8 m. A = 11 × 6 = 66 m cuadrados. Usa siempre la altura perpendicular, no el lado inclinado.
hintsEs: Mira el Paso 3. ¿Cuál valor debe usarse para h — el lado inclinado o la altura?
La altura debe ser perpendicular a la base. El lado inclinado no es la altura.

onLevel.prompt: A parallelogram has a base of 12 cm. If you double the height, the area doubles too. Explain why this happens using the formula, and give a specific example with numbers.
onLevel.sentenceFrame: When the height doubles from ___ to ___, the area changes from ___ to ___ because in the formula A = b × h, the base stays at ___ and ___.
onLevel.hint: Pick a starting height; use A = base x height to see what happens.
hints: The base stays 12 cm the whole time — only the height changes. Your explanation should lean on A = b × h.
Pick an easy starting height (like 5 cm), find the area, then double the height to 10 cm and find the new area.
Compute 12 × 5, then 12 × 10. Describe what happened to the area when the height doubled, using the word 'multiply'.
onLevel.explanation: In A = b × h the base of 12 cm is a fixed factor, so the area is just 12 times whatever the height is. With h = 5, A = 12 × 5 = 60 sq cm; doubling to h = 10 gives A = 12 × 10 = 120 sq cm, exactly double, because doubling one factor doubles the product.
onLevel.explanationEs: En A = b × h la base de 12 cm es un factor fijo, así que el área es simplemente 12 veces la altura que tengas. Con h = 5, A = 12 × 5 = 60 sq cm; al duplicar a h = 10 queda A = 12 × 10 = 120 sq cm, exactamente el doble, porque duplicar un factor duplica el producto.
onLevel.promptEs: Un paralelogramo tiene una base de 12 cm. Si duplicas la altura, el área también se duplica. Explica por qué pasa esto usando la fórmula y da un ejemplo específico con números.
hintsEs: La base se queda en 12 cm todo el tiempo; solo cambia la altura. Tu explicación debe apoyarse en A = b × h.
Escoge una altura inicial fácil (como 5 cm), halla el área, luego duplica la altura a 10 cm y halla el área nueva.
Calcula 12 × 5 y luego 12 × 10. Describe qué le pasó al área cuando la altura se duplicó, usando la palabra 'multiplicar'.

onLevel.stem: Cut the slanted end off a parallelogram and slide it to the other side. What shape forms, and why does that show A = base × height?
choices: A rectangle with the same base and height, so its area equals base x height
A bigger parallelogram, so the area gets larger
A triangle, so the area is cut in half
A square, so all four sides must be equal
onLevel.explanation: Sliding the cut triangle turns the parallelogram into a rectangle that keeps the same base and height. A rectangle's area is base x height, so the parallelogram's area is base x height too.
choiceFeedback: Does cutting and moving a piece change how much space is covered?
The rearranged shape still has the same area as before.
After rearranging, do you have three sides or four?
onLevel.stemEs: Corta el extremo inclinado de un paralelogramo y deslízalo al otro lado. ¿Qué figura se forma y por qué eso muestra que A = base × altura?
onLevel.explanationEs: Deslizar el triángulo cortado convierte el paralelogramo en un rectángulo que conserva la misma base y la misma altura. El área de un rectángulo es base × altura, así que el área del paralelogramo también es base × altura.
hints: Cutting a piece off and sliding it somewhere else moves the surface around but does not add or remove any of it.
Picture the new outline after the triangle slides over: think about whether the corners become square.
The base along the bottom never changes, and the straight-up height never changes either. Ask yourself which familiar shape has those exact two measurements and square corners.
hintsEs: Cortar una parte y deslizarla a otro lugar mueve la superficie, pero no añade ni quita nada de ella.
Imagina el nuevo contorno después de deslizar el triángulo: piensa si las esquinas quedan rectas.
La base de abajo no cambia, y la altura vertical tampoco cambia. Pregúntate qué figura conocida tiene esas dos medidas exactas y esquinas rectas.
choicesEs: Un rectángulo con la misma base y la misma altura, así que su área es igual a base × altura
Un paralelogramo más grande, así que el área aumenta
Un triángulo, así que el área se reduce a la mitad
Un cuadrado, así que los cuatro lados deben ser iguales

extending.stem: A blueprint parallelogram has a base of 8 ft, a height of 5 ft, and a slanted side of 7 ft. What is its area?
extending.explanation: Area = base x height = 8 x 5 = 40 sq ft. The 7 ft slanted side is not used; only the perpendicular height belongs in the formula.
choiceFeedback: Use the perpendicular height (5 ft), not the slant side (7 ft).
Height times slant is not the formula; use base times height.
Which measurement is perpendicular to the base?
extending.stemEs: Un paralelogramo de un plano tiene una base de 8 ft, una altura de 5 ft y un lado inclinado de 7 ft. ¿Cuál es su área?
extending.explanationEs: Área = base × altura = 8 × 5 = 40 pies cuadrados. El lado inclinado de 7 ft no se usa; solo la altura perpendicular entra en la fórmula.
hints: Not every measurement in a problem belongs in the formula — area only needs a base and its perpendicular height.
Identify which of the three numbers describes the straight-up distance, then leave the slanted side out entirely.
The base is 8 ft and the perpendicular height is 5 ft. Multiply those two and label the result in square feet.
hintsEs: No toda medida de un problema pertenece a la fórmula: el área solo necesita una base y su altura perpendicular.
Identifica cuál de los tres números describe la distancia vertical y deja el lado inclinado completamente fuera.
La base es 8 ft y la altura perpendicular es 5 ft. Multiplica esas dos y etiqueta el resultado en pies cuadrados.

extending.stem: Two parallelograms both have base 10 ft and height 6 ft. N is more tilted (slant 9 ft). Compare their areas.
choices: Equal: both are 10 x 6 = 60 sq ft because area depends on base and height, not the slant
Blueprint N is larger because its slanted side is 9 ft
Blueprint M is larger because it is less tilted
You cannot compare them without the slanted side of M
extending.explanation: Area = base x height. Both have base 10 ft and height 6 ft, so both areas are 10 x 6 = 60 sq ft. Tilting the shape changes the slanted side but not the perpendicular height, so the area stays the same.
choiceFeedback: If base and height do not change, does area change?
Tilting the shape changes the slant, not the perpendicular height.
Does the formula A = base x height depend on the slant?
extending.stemEs: Dos paralelogramos tienen base 10 ft y altura 6 ft. N está más inclinado (lado inclinado de 9 ft). Compara sus áreas.
extending.explanationEs: Área = base × altura. Ambos tienen base 10 ft y altura 6 ft, así que ambas áreas son 10 × 6 = 60 pies cuadrados. Inclinar la figura cambia el lado inclinado, pero no la altura perpendicular, así que el área se mantiene igual.
hints: The area formula only takes in two measurements: the base and the perpendicular height.
Check whether either of those two measurements is different between the shapes before deciding anything about tilt.
Both shapes report base 10 ft and height 6 ft, so run 10 × 6 for each one and see what that tells you about the comparison.
hintsEs: La fórmula del área solo usa dos medidas: la base y la altura perpendicular.
Revisa si alguna de esas dos medidas es distinta entre las figuras antes de decidir algo sobre la inclinación.
Ambas figuras tienen base 10 ft y altura 6 ft, así que calcula 10 × 6 para cada una y observa qué te dice esa comparación.
choicesEs: Iguales: los dos son 10 × 6 = 60 pies cuadrados, porque el área depende de la base y la altura, no de la inclinación
El plano N es más grande porque su lado inclinado mide 9 pies
El plano M es más grande porque está menos inclinado
No se pueden comparar sin el lado inclinado de M

extending.title: Level 2 Extension — The Slanted-Side Slip-Up

workedExample.label: Read the blueprint
workedExample.work: base = 12 ft, slanted side = 10 ft, height = 7 ft
workedExample.workEs: base = 12 pies, lado inclinado = 10 pies, altura = 7 pies

extending.correctWork: The height is 7 ft, not the slanted side of 10 ft. Substitute the perpendicular height: A = 12 x 7 = 84 sq ft. Only the straight-up height belongs in A = base x height.
hints: Look at the substitution step. Which number did the designer plug in for the height -- the slanted side or the real height?
The height must be perpendicular (a 90 degree angle) to the base. The 10 ft slanted side is not the height, so use 7 ft instead.
extending.titleEs: Extensión Nivel 2 — El desliz del lado inclinado
extending.explanation: The blueprint lists three numbers, and the substitution step grabs the 10 ft slanted side instead of the 7 ft height. Since A = base × height only accepts the perpendicular measurement, the real area is A = 12 × 7 = 84 sq ft.
extending.explanationEs: El plano da tres números, y el paso de sustitución toma el lado inclinado de 10 ft en lugar de la altura de 7 ft. Como A = base × altura solo acepta la medida perpendicular, el área real es A = 12 × 7 = 84 sq ft.
extending.correctWorkEs: La altura es 7 pies, no el lado inclinado de 10 pies. Sustituye la altura perpendicular: A = 12 × 7 = 84 pies cuadrados. Solo la altura recta va en A = base × altura.
hintsEs: Mira el paso de sustitución. ¿Qué número usó el diseñador para la altura — el lado inclinado o la altura real?
La altura debe ser perpendicular (un ángulo de 90 grados) a la base. El lado inclinado de 10 pies no es la altura, así que usa 7 pies.

extending.stem: What is the area of a parallelogram with base 10 cm and height 7 cm?
choiceFeedback: Did you add? The formula multiplies base and height.
You found 10 + 7; try multiplying instead.
That label measures a distance along a line, but area describes the flat region a shape covers. Multiplying two lengths always produces square units.
hints: You know both the base (10 cm) and the height (7 cm) — this is a direct use of the parallelogram area formula.
Area of a parallelogram is A = base × height. Adding the two numbers gives perimeter-style thinking, not area.
Set up A = 10 × 7 and multiply. Label your result in square centimeters.
extending.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el área de un paralelogramo con base 10 cm y altura 7 cm?
hintsEs: Conoces tanto la base (10 cm) como la altura (7 cm): este es un uso directo de la fórmula del área del paralelogramo.
El área de un paralelogramo es A = base × altura. Sumar los dos números es pensar en perímetro, no en área.
Plantea A = 10 × 7 y multiplica. Escribe tu resultado en centímetros cuadrados.

extending.stem: A parallelogram has an area of 54 sq ft and a base of 9 ft. What is the height?
choiceFeedback: Work backwards: if A = b × h and A = 54, h = 54 ÷ 9.
54 + 9 is too large for the height.
Is the height half of 54?
hints: This time you're given the area (54 sq ft) and the base (9 ft) — the height is the missing piece.
Start from A = b × h. To undo a multiplication, divide: h = A ÷ b.
Write 54 = 9 × h, then divide 54 by 9 to find the height in feet.
extending.stemEs: Un paralelogramo tiene un área de 54 pies cuadrados y una base de 9 ft. ¿Cuál es la altura?
hintsEs: Esta vez te dan el área (54 pies²) y la base (9 pies): la altura es la pieza que falta.
Empieza con A = b × h. Para deshacer una multiplicación, divide: h = A ÷ b.
Escribe 54 = 9 × h y luego divide 54 entre 9 para hallar la altura en pies.

extending.stem: What is the area of a parallelogram with base 9 cm and height 5 cm?
choiceFeedback: Add base and height? The formula multiplies them.
You added 9 + 5; try multiplying.
22.5 is half of 45; is that the area formula?
hints: Spot the base (9 cm) and the height (5 cm). Which operation does the area formula use on them?
Use A = base × height. If your number looks like 9 + 5, or like half the product, rethink the operation.
Compute 9 × 5 and give the answer in square centimeters.
extending.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el área de un paralelogramo con base 9 cm y altura 5 cm?
hintsEs: Identifica la base (9 cm) y la altura (5 cm). ¿Qué operación usa la fórmula del área con ellas?
Usa A = base × altura. Si tu número se parece a 9 + 5, o a la mitad del producto, repiensa la operación.
Calcula 9 × 5 y da la respuesta en centímetros cuadrados.

extending.stem: Which measurement is the height of a parallelogram?
choices: The perpendicular distance between the base and the opposite side
The length of the slanted side
extending.explanation: The height is always the perpendicular (straight up-and-down) distance between the base and the opposite side, not the slanted side.
choiceFeedback: The slanted side is not perpendicular to the base.
Perimeter is around the shape; height is perpendicular distance.
The longest side is not always the height.
hints: Picture a leaning parallelogram. The height is not a side you can trace — it's a distance measured straight across.
Height must make a right angle (90°) with the base. Test each choice: is this perpendicular to the base?
Draw a base, then a straight up-and-down dashed line to the opposite side. That dashed line is what 'height' means here.
extending.stemEs: ¿Cuál medida es la altura de un paralelogramo?
extending.explanationEs: La altura siempre es la distancia perpendicular (recta, de arriba abajo) entre la base y el lado opuesto, no el lado inclinado.
choicesEs: La distancia perpendicular entre la base y el lado opuesto
hintsEs: Imagina un paralelogramo inclinado. La altura no es un lado que puedas trazar: es una distancia medida en línea recta.
La altura debe formar un ángulo recto (90°) con la base. Prueba cada opción: ¿es perpendicular a la base?
Dibuja una base y luego una línea punteada recta hacia arriba hasta el lado opuesto. Esa línea punteada es lo que significa 'altura' aquí.

extending.hint: Use A = b x h to find area; use h = A / b to find missing height.
hints: Check each row: Patios A and D are missing area, but Patios B and C are missing a base or a height.
Missing area → multiply b × h. Missing base or height → divide the area by the measurement you know.
For Patio B: 56 = 8 × h, so divide 56 by 8. For Patio A, multiply 14 × 9.
extending.explanation: Patios A and D give both measurements, so multiply: 14 × 9 = 126 sq ft and 15 × 6 = 90 sq ft. Patios B and C give the area and one measurement, so divide to undo the multiplication: 56 ÷ 8 = 7 ft of height and 96 ÷ 12 = 8 ft of base.
extending.explanationEs: Los Patios A y D dan las dos medidas, así que multiplicas: 14 × 9 = 126 sq ft y 15 × 6 = 90 sq ft. Los Patios B y C dan el área y una medida, así que divides para deshacer la multiplicación: 56 ÷ 8 = 7 ft de altura y 96 ÷ 12 = 8 ft de base.
hintsEs: Revisa cada fila: a los Patios A y D les falta el área, pero a los Patios B y C les falta una base o una altura.
Falta el área → multiplica b × h. Falta la base o la altura → divide el área entre la medida que sí conoces.
Para el Patio B: 56 = 8 × h, así que divide 56 entre 8. Para el Patio A, multiplica 14 × 9.

practice.commonMistake: The most common mistake in Area of Parallelograms is multiplying the base by the slanted side instead of the perpendicular height. For a parallelogram with a base of 16 ft, a perpendicular height of 9 ft, and a slanted side of 11 ft, students compute 16 × 11 = 176 square feet instead of the correct 16 × 9 = 144 square feet. The height must be the straight-up (perpendicular) distance between the base and its opposite side, not the length of the slanted side, even though the slanted side is often the number that 'looks' like it belongs in the formula.

connect.scenario: A landscape architect is tiling a parallelogram-shaped courtyard. The courtyard has a base of 18 feet and a height of 10 feet. Each tile covers 2 square feet.
connect.promptQuestion: How many tiles does the architect need?
connect.prompt: The courtyard's area is ___ sq ft because A = ___ x ___ . She needs ___ tiles because ___ / 2 = ___.

check.stem: What is the area of the parallelogram courtyard?
check.explanation: A = base × height = 18 × 10 = 180 sq ft. Use the perpendicular height, not a slanted side.

check.stem: How many tiles does the architect need?
check.explanation: Each tile covers 2 sq ft, so 180 ÷ 2 = 90 tiles.

check.stem: Why use the height instead of the slanted side length?
choices: Because area needs the perpendicular distance between the two bases
Because the slanted side is always longer
Because the base is on the bottom
check.explanation: Sliding the end triangle over turns a parallelogram into a rectangle whose sides are the base and the perpendicular height — that is why A = b × h.

connect.modelAnswer: A = base × height = 18 × 10 = 180 sq ft. Each tile covers 2 sq ft, so the architect needs 180 ÷ 2 = 90 tiles. Use the perpendicular height (10 ft), not a slanted side.

exitTicket.stem: Explain your thinking — A parallelogram has a base of 13 inches and a height of 5 inches. What is its area?
exitTicket.explanation: A = b x h = 13 x 5 = 65 square inches.
choiceFeedback: Area of a parallelogram is base × height, not adding sides.
That looks like base + height — multiply them instead.
Right number, wrong unit — area is measured in square inches.
hints: You have a base of 13 inches and a height of 5 inches — both numbers the parallelogram formula needs.
Use A = b × h, and remember area is measured in square inches, not plain inches.
Multiply 13 × 5 (try 10 × 5 plus 3 × 5) and label the result in square inches.

warmup.spiralFrom: Area of rectangles and square units

questions.stem: What is the area of a rectangle 9 cm long and 5 cm wide?
questions.explanation: Area multiplies the two side lengths: 9 × 5 = 45 square cm. 28 is the distance around the rectangle, which is perimeter.

questions.stem: Area is always measured in which kind of unit?
questions.explanation: Area counts the squares that cover a surface, so it is reported in square units. Cubic units fill a space.

questions.stem: A rectangle has an area of 54 square feet and one side measures 9 feet. How long is the other side?
questions.explanation: Area is one side times the other, so divide to undo it: 54 ÷ 9 = 6 feet.

questions.stem: In a rectangle, the height is measured how?
choices: Straight up from the base, at a right angle
questions.explanation: Height is always perpendicular to the base — it meets it at a right angle. Corner to corner is a diagonal.
